h: NCC warns 'London-used' phones may be cut off if they fail device checks
p: Imported used phones flagged by the Nigerian Communications Commission could lose network service after 30 days, under its device checker rules. The regulator has been sending text alerts to affected users since October.
body: Nigerians who buy imported used phones, popularly called 'London-used', could reportedly lose mobile service if their devices fail checks by the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC).
Under the regulator's Device Checker and Type Approval Compliance framework, flagged devices may be disconnected from local networks after 30 cumulative days.

The NCC began sending text alerts under the sender name NCC-Checker on 10 October 2026. The messages advise affected users to contact the seller or check their device using the regulator's device checker. Alerts have reportedly gone to users of iPhones, Google Pixels, TECNO, Infinix and other brands.
About 231 million devices that were already active on Nigerian networks before the rollout were captured automatically.
more: Flagged phones may be cut off after 30 days.
About 231 million existing devices were captured automatically.
